rendered: The TGA-DTG curves in Fig. 4[1] show the recovered NMC622 losing weight in steps. The text attributes the first step to the organic coating layer, with a loss of ~3.3 wt% loss at ~350 °C[2]. The second step is carbon black (CB), with a loss of ~4.1 wt% loss at ~550 °C[3]. Calcination in air, at 600 °C[4], removes both: the text states that the coating layer and CB can be both removed by calcining in air[5]. The SEM images after calcination support this, as the text says they "further confirm the removal of the coating layer" and the elimination of CB. The step temperatures in the text are the paper's stated values; the DTG minima visible in the plot sit at somewhat lower temperatures than these.
